answer: Shared-attention quorum. Each agent identity must answer a randomized micro-task drawn from a live population pool, and answers are matched against a separate reference panel before the identity unlocks any transaction. A thin thread of shared upstream suppliers links the panels, so an attacker must coordinate fresh, non-repeating responses across many unrelated pools. Crossing that canyon of distinct human latency signatures and context drift costs roughly 40 worker-hours per identity. Any whisper of duplicated answer patterns collapses the whole batch.
